stories.headline: IRAN RESPONDS TO US CEASEFIRE PROPOSAL: NUCLEAR PROGRAM AND FULL SANCTIONS RELIEF NOW ON THE TABLE
stories.body: Iran delivered its formal response to Washington's ceasefire proposal on May 10, demanding negotiations cover a permanent end to the war on all fronts — including Lebanon — alongside shipping security and Iran's nuclear program. Tehran wants sanctions relief discussions fully in scope while deferring enrichment limits to a later phase; Washington has insisted enrichment limits must be in any MOU. A drone ignited a small fire on a ship off Qatar today, testing the ceasefire even as Trump said 'it's very possible we'll make a deal.' The May 31 deadline holds.

stories.headline: OIL HOLDS NEAR $95 WTI AS DRONE OFF QATAR REINFORCES CEASEFIRE FRAGILITY DESPITE IRAN RESPONSE
stories.body: WTI closed Friday at $95.46 and Brent at $100.54, with Sunday's drone incident off Qatar reinforcing market skepticism about a near-term Hormuz resolution. Iran's nuclear-program inclusion in its ceasefire response creates a new sticking point that extends the deal timeline beyond May 31. Analysts estimate a credible resolution would send WTI back toward $78-82, removing the entire $10-15 geopolitical risk premium currently embedded in the forward curve.

stories.headline: APRIL PAYROLLS CRUSH ESTIMATES: 115K JOBS ADDED VS. 62K FORECAST
stories.body: The U.S. economy added 115,000 jobs in April — nearly double the 62K consensus — while March was revised up to 185K. Wage growth softened to 3.6% YoY (vs. 3.8% expected), moderating the bond selloff. The data is Warsh's first major test as Fed Chair and drives CME hike odds to 38.5% for the next 12 months, cementing higher-for-longer through at least Q4 2027.

stories.headline: AMD +16% ON 57% DATA CENTER SURGE, LIFTING AI INFRASTRUCTURE TRADE TO ALL-TIME HIGHS
stories.body: AMD reported Q1 revenue of $10.25B (+38% YoY) with data center sales of $5.8B (+57%), driven by the Instinct MI400 AI GPU line. Shares surged 16-19% on the week to $415, lifting Nvidia (+2%) and SMCI (+13%) to fresh records. The S&P 500 hit 7,392 Friday — a sixth straight weekly gain — with AI infrastructure a primary driver of the 2026 equity rally. AMD guides Q2 revenue to $11.2B (+46% YoY).

stories.headline: NCAA VOTES UNANIMOUSLY TO EXPAND MARCH MADNESS TO 76 TEAMS STARTING 2027
stories.body: Both men's and women's tournament committees voted unanimously this week to expand the field from 68 to 76 teams beginning in 2026-27. The new Opening Round adds 12 games over two days before the traditional First Four, unlocking $131M in additional revenue distributions funded by new beer, wine, and spirits sponsorship deals — a first for the NCAA. Michigan won the 2026 men's title; the expanded 76-team bracket tips off March 2027.

stories.headline: CAVALIERS AVOID 3-0 HOLE WITH MITCHELL'S 35-PT GAME 3 WIN; OKC LEADS LAKERS 3-0; KNICKS SEEK SWEEP TODAY
stories.body: Donovan Mitchell erupted for 35 points and 10 rebounds as Cleveland beat Detroit 116-109 in Game 3 (May 9) to cut the Pistons' series lead to 2-1. James Harden was clutch with 7 of his 19 points in the final 90 seconds; Cade Cunningham triple-doubled (27/10/10) in the loss. OKC destroyed LA 131-108 to go up 3-0 in the West. The Knicks entered Game 4 today (3:30 ET, ABC) looking to sweep Philly 4-0; Spurs-Wolves Game 4 tips at 7:30 ET (SAS leads 2-1).

stories.headline: SEAHAWKS ROOKIE MINICAMP UNDERWAY; RELEASE CAM AKERS, SIGN TE HARRISON BRYANT AHEAD OF MAY 14 SCHEDULE DROP
stories.body: The Super Bowl champion Seahawks kicked off rookie minicamp at VMAC this weekend, signing six of their eight 2026 draft picks and adding seven undrafted free agents. The team released veteran RB Cam Akers and signed TE Harrison Bryant to deepen the tight end room behind Noah Fant. The full 2026 schedule — 17 games across all 32 teams — releases Thursday May 14 at 8 PM ET on NFL Network and ESPN2; Seattle hosts the league opener Sept. 9 on NBC. OTAs begin May 26.

stories.headline: TEXAS TECH QB BRENDAN SORSBY UNDER GAMBLING PROBE; CFP PROJECTIONS HAVE TEXAS ATOP EARLY POLLS
stories.body: Texas Tech's depth chart is unsettled after news of a gambling investigation involving starter Brendan Sorsby, adding pre-fall uncertainty to the Red Raiders. CBS Sports' updated CFP projections place Texas atop early polls with Arch Manning healthy, while Notre Dame and BYU stand out as the only two FBS programs returning at least 60% of defensive snaps across all three position groups — a notable durability edge entering fall camp.

deepDive.title: Sanctions Unwind — What Lifting Iran Sanctions Would Actually Do to Global Oil Supply
content: Iran delivered its formal ceasefire response today, explicitly putting nuclear program talks and sanctions relief on the negotiating table. Oil markets largely shrugged — WTI sits at $95 and Brent near $100 — because both sides remain far apart on enrichment limits, and a drone off Qatar today reinforced ceasefire fragility. But the stakes of a deal are enormous: sanctions removal doesn't simply reopen a strait, it restructures how approximately 2-3 million barrels per day of crude reaches global markets. Understanding that mechanism tells you more about the deal's oil price impact than any headline about 'peace prospects.'

Iran officially produces roughly 3.2 million barrels per day but under sanctions moves the excess through a shadow fleet — tankers with opaque ownership, falsified manifests, and AIS transponders that go dark en route to Chinese ports. Nearly all sanctioned Iranian crude flows to China at a $5-10 per barrel discount to Brent, insulating Tehran from the worst of the restrictions at the cost of market access and price realization. Sanctions relief would dissolve this discount: Iranian barrels would re-enter official channels, becoming eligible for SWIFT-cleared payments, indexed to Brent rather than sold at negotiated discounts, and marketable to India, Europe, and Asia simultaneously. That re-pricing adds $5-10 per barrel to Iranian export revenue even before any production ramp — a direct incentive for Tehran to push for sanctions relief over enrichment concessions.

The 2015 JCPOA is the historical template, and the numbers are instructive. When sanctions were lifted in January 2016, Iran ramped production from approximately 2.7 to 3.8 million barrels per day within 18 months — the fastest ramp of any OPEC member in a decade — contributing materially to the 2015-16 global supply glut that helped crater Brent from $65 to $27 by February 2016. Today's scenario differs: a decade of underinvestment, sanctions-era infrastructure deterioration, and uncertain reservoir pressure have degraded Iran's surge capacity. Energy Aspects and Goldman estimate a realistic 0.5-1.0 mb/d incremental supply addition over 6-18 months, not the 1.1 mb/d seen post-JCPOA. But even 0.5 mb/d of new supply in a market already carrying a $10-15 geopolitical premium is structurally significant.

For the current market setup, the math is relatively clean: a credible deal removes the risk premium and adds incremental supply, sending WTI toward $78-82 — a $13-17 decline from current levels. At roughly $0.03 per barrel of pass-through to retail gasoline, that's a $0.40-0.50 reduction at the pump, which at current U.S. consumption rates subtracts approximately 0.35-0.45 percentage points from annualized headline CPI. That is the disinflationary window Fed Chair Warsh needs to hold rates steady at the June 17-18 FOMC without signaling a capitulation on inflation credibility. The sticking point — Washington insisting enrichment limits be in any MOU while Tehran wants them deferred — is why the probability of a deal by May 31 remains below 30%, and why the full $10-15 risk premium persists in the forward curve even as both sides say they want peace.
